payload.task: Self-diffusion coefficient of Cu in a perfect fcc Cu crystal at 300 K by molecular dynamics (request 19e33521, need #0)
payload.reason: Premise check failed: this property can't be measured with MD at this temperature and timescale. (1) A perfect crystal has no vacancies or interstitials, so there is no diffusion mechanism. A periodic MD cell stays defect-free unless a Frenkel pair forms spontaneously, which takes several eV and does not happen at 300 K. The atoms just vibrate, so the MSD levels off at about 3<u^2> ~ 0.02 A^2 and any slope fitted to it is noise or thermostat/COM drift, not diffusion. (2) Even in real Cu, which has thermal vacancies, the 300 K value is far too small to see. Extrapolating the measured 64Cu tracer Arrhenius law (Krautheim et al. 1979, D0 = 0.68 (+0.16/-0.12) cm2/s, Q = 2.17 +/- 0.02 eV, measured at 1078-1348 K) gives D(300 K) ~ 2e-37 cm2/s (about 1e-37 to 6e-37 within the stated D0/Q uncertainty alone). The extrapolation goes ~800 K beyond the data, so the real uncertainty is orders of magnitude. At that D an atom makes about one nearest-neighbour-distance displacement every ~1e13 years. MD covers ns to us. (3) The equilibrium vacancy fraction at 300 K is exp(-~1.28 eV/kT) ~ 3e-22, so any tractable MD cell (1e3-1e6 atoms) contains zero vacancies. A number computed this way would be an artefact, so I am not running it. Well-posed alternatives (each can be validated against the high-T tracer data above): (a) put one vacancy in a ~500-2000 atom fcc Cu cell (EAM, e.g. Mishin 2001, or an MLIP such as MACE-MP), run NVT MD at 1000-1300 K, and get D_vac from the vacancy MSD. Then D_self = f * c_v * D_vac with correlation factor f = 0.7815 and c_v = exp(S_f/k) exp(-E_f/kT) from the same model. Check against the Krautheim D0/Q in 1078-1348 K first, then extrapolate to 300 K only as an Arrhenius estimate with an explicitly orders-of-magnitude uncertainty. (b) A static route: E_f from relaxation and E_m from NEB, giving Q = E_f + E_m, compared with the measured 2.17 eV. (c) If a directly measurable MD diffusion coefficient is what's wanted, use liquid Cu just above T_m = 1357.77 K (ITS-90, /data/calibration/tier1.json), where D ~ 1e-5 cm2/s is reachable in ~100 ps runs, validated against measured liquid-Cu self-diffusion.

details.premise_check: failed - no diffusion mechanism in a defect-free lattice; D(300 K) far below any MD detection limit
details.estimate_basis: Arrhenius extrapolation of 64Cu tracer data, Krautheim et al., Kristall und Technik 14 (1979), doi:10.1002/crat.19790141216: D0 = 0.68 (+0.16/-0.12) cm2/s, Q0 = 2.17 +/- 0.02 eV, 1078-1348 K
details.estimate_caveat: Extrapolated ~800 K below the measured range; divacancy curvature and short-circuit (dislocation/grain-boundary) paths in real samples dominate at low T; not a measurable quantity, order-of-magnitude context only
details.md_detection_limit_note: With a 1 us run and ~1e4 atoms, sqrt(6Dt) ~ 1e-13 A, ~13 orders of magnitude below vibrational amplitude
